/-- **The unit relation `res x · res y = 1` on the overlap (route step 3).**  Both
restrictions factor, by `res_p1XSection`/`res_p1YSection`, through the common overlap
ring map `toProjInt.appLE D₊(X₀X₁)`, whence the product is the pullback of
`awayToSection (awayMap(X₁/X₀) · awayMap(X₀/X₁))`; the away-ring identity
`awayMap_coord_mul_eq_one` collapses the argument to `1`. -/
private lemma p1_res_x_mul_res_y (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    ((ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin 2); Spec (CommRingCat.of k))).presheaf.map
        (homOfLE (inf_le_left : p1Chart k ⟨0⟩ ⊓ p1Chart k ⟨1⟩ ≤ p1Chart k ⟨0⟩)).op).hom
      (p1XSection k)
      * ((ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin 2); Spec (CommRingCat.of k))).presheaf.map
          (homOfLE (inf_le_right : p1Chart k ⟨0⟩ ⊓ p1Chart k ⟨1⟩ ≤ p1Chart k ⟨1⟩)).op).hom
        (p1YSection k)
      = 1 := by
  rw [res_p1XSection k, res_p1YSection k, ← map_mul, ← map_mul,
    awayMap_coord_mul_eq_one, map_one, map_one]

/-- **The `ℙ¹` Laurent chart datum (route step 4, assembly).**  On the standard 2-chart
geometry `p1CoverSquare` of `ℙ¹ = ℙ(ULift (Fin 2); Spec k)` (charts `V₀ = p1Chart ⟨0⟩`,
`V₁ = p1Chart ⟨1⟩`, coordinates `x = p1XSection`, `y = p1YSection`), the chart-ring
computation assembles into the `Adelic.LaurentChartData` consumed by the keystone:
the overlap is the basic open of either coordinate (`p1Chart_inf_eq_basicOpen_coordSection`),
the coordinates are mutually inverse (`p1_res_x_mul_res_y`), and each chart ring is the
`k`-span of the powers of its coordinate (`span_pow_p1XSection_scaffold`,
`span_pow_p1YSection_scaffold`). -/
noncomputable def p1LaurentChartData (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    LaurentChartData
      (Over.mk (ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin 2); Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) where
  V₀ := p1Chart k ⟨0⟩
  V₁ := p1Chart k ⟨1⟩
  isAffineOpen_V₀ := isAffineOpen_p1Chart k ⟨0⟩
  isAffineOpen_V₁ := isAffineOpen_p1Chart k ⟨1⟩
  cover := p1Chart_sup_eq_top k
  x := p1XSection k
  y := p1YSection k
  inf_eq_basicOpen_x := p1Chart_inf_eq_basicOpen_coordSection k ⟨0⟩ ⟨1⟩
  inf_eq_basicOpen_y := by
    rw [inf_comm]
    exact p1Chart_inf_eq_basicOpen_coordSection k ⟨1⟩ ⟨0⟩
  res_x_mul_res_y := p1_res_x_mul_res_y k
  span_pow_x := span_pow_p1XSection_scaffold k
  span_pow_y := span_pow_p1YSection_scaffold k

/-- **Gate #1 of the genus theorem discharged.**  The concrete projective line
`ℙ(ULift (Fin 2); Spec k)` carries Laurent chart data (`p1LaurentChartData`), so the
`Adelic.P1HasLaurentChartData` gate holds for every field `k` — the char-free Route B
of the module header, closing node `N11b`. -/
noncomputable instance instP1HasLaurentChartData (k : Type u) [Field k] :
    P1HasLaurentChartData k :=
  ⟨⟨p1LaurentChartData k⟩⟩

end Overlap

end AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic

8	/-!
9	# Genus finiteness of the curve (node `N12`, the adelic lane's consumable)
10	
11	This file is part of the **adelic Riemann–Roch lane**.  It composes the two halves
12	of the lane that are now proved:
13	
14	* the **keystone** `Adelic.module_finite_hModule_one_of_finite_map`
15	  (`FinitenessP1.lean`, node `N11`): under the gates `HasFiniteMapToP1 C` and
16	  `P1HasLaurentChartData k`, *some* 2-affine cover `S` of `C` (the pullback of the
17	  standard ℙ¹ charts along the finite map) has finite-dimensional Čech cokernel
18	  `Ȟ¹ = S.H1Cok`, so any comparison `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) ≃ₗ[k] S.H1Cok` transports the
19	  finiteness to the genus carrier;
20	* the **comparison** `AffineCoverMVSquare.hModuleOneEquivH1Cok`
21	  (`Cokernel.lean`, nodes `N5` + `N6`): for *every* 2-affine cover `S`, under the
22	  Čech-to-derived gate `HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily`,
23	  `HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1 ≃ₗ[k] S.H1Cok (toModuleKSheaf C)` — the N5 half
24	  (`cechCohomology 1 ≃ₗ H1Cok`) is unconditional, only the N6 half is gated.
25	
26	## The honest gate set
27	
28	The keystone produces an *existential* cover (`D.pullbackSquare π` for a chosen
29	finite `π` and chart data `D`), which cannot be named in a theorem signature; the
30	comparison must therefore be available for **all** 2-affine covers, i.e. the honest
31	Čech-to-derived hypothesis is the `∀`-quantified instance gate
32	`[∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily]` (a `Prop`-class
33	hypothesis with no sorried instance, in the `HasPicScheme`/`HasFiniteMapToP1`
34	gating pattern).  The full gate set of the consumable is
35	
36	* `HasFiniteMapToP1 C` — node `N9`; derived in `FiniteMapToP1.lean` from the single
37	  strictly weaker gate `ExistsNonconstantMapToP1 C` under the ambient curve
38	  hypotheses;
39	* `P1HasLaurentChartData k` — node `N11b`, the ℙ¹ chart-ring computation
40	  (`P1ChartData.lean` is building towards its instance);
41	* `HasExt.{u}`/`HasExt.{u+1}` — the ambient `Ext`-theory instances the `HModule`
42	  machinery runs on;
43	* `∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily` — the Čech-to-derived
44	  comparison (Leray/Cartan) for 2-affine covers of the curve.
45	
46	Under these, the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1` is a
47	finite-dimensional `k`-vector space, so `genus C = finrank k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is an
48	honest natural number.
49	-/
50	
51	universe u
52	
53	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
54	
55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic
56	
57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
58	
59	/-- **Genus finiteness of the curve (node `N12`, gated).**  For a curve `C` over `k`
60	with a finite morphism to ℙ¹ and the ℙ¹ chart data, and with the Čech-to-derived
61	comparison available on 2-affine covers, the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite
62	`k`-module.  Composes the `N11` keystone `module_finite_hModule_one_of_finite_map`
63	with the `N5`+`N6` comparison `hModuleOneEquivH1Cok` of `Cokernel.lean`. -/
64	theorem module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1
65	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] [P1HasLaurentChartData k]
66	    [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
67	    [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
68	    [∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare,
69	      HasCechToHModuleIso (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily] :
70	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 1) :=
71	  module_finite_hModule_one_of_finite_map C
72	    (fun S => ⟨S.hModuleOneEquivH1Cok (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C)⟩)
73	
74	end AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.GenusFiniteness
7	
8	/-!
9	# The last genus-finiteness gates: scoping the Čech-to-derived comparison
10	
11	This file scopes the **final** gates of the adelic genus-finiteness consumable
12	`Adelic.module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1` (`GenusFiniteness.lean`, node `N12`).
13	That consumable is stated under four gates:
14	
15	1. `HasFiniteMapToP1 C`               — node `N9`  (curve ⟶ ℙ¹, in progress elsewhere);
16	2. `P1HasLaurentChartData k`          — node `N11b` (ℙ¹ chart rings, `P1ChartData.lean`);
17	3. `HasExt.{u}` **and** `HasExt.{u+1}` for the sheaf category
18	   `Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)`
19	   — the ambient `Ext`-theory the `HModule` genus carrier runs on;
20	4. `∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare,
21	      HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily`
22	   — the Čech-to-derived comparison (Leray/Cartan) on 2-affine covers.
23	
24	The question this file answers: **are gates 3 and 4 instantiable today?**
25	
26	## Gate 3 (the `HasExt` pair): INSTANTIABLE — proved here
27	
28	The genus carrier lives in the sheaf category `𝒮 := Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology
29	C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)`, i.e. sheaves of `k`-modules for the *constant* base
30	field `k`.  This is the crucial point that dissolves the historical blocker: `𝒮` is a
31	**Grothendieck abelian category** (Mathlib `IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} (Sheaf J A)` for a
32	small site `J` and Grothendieck-abelian `A = ModuleCat k`), so Mathlib supplies
33	`EnoughInjectives 𝒮` (`079H`) and both `HasExt.{u} 𝒮`, `HasExt.{u+1} 𝒮` (`HasExt.standard`)
34	**for free**.  See `hasExt_moduleKSheaf` / `hasExt_succ_moduleKSheaf` /
35	`enoughInjectives_moduleKSheaf` / `isGrothendieckAbelian_moduleKSheaf` below.
36	
37	This is *not* the situation of the `SheafOfModules R = X.Modules` apparatus (`Ext` over the
38	structure sheaf `𝒪_X` as a sheaf of rings), which the historical Čech capstone
39	(`CechToCohomology.cech_eq_cohomology_of_basis`, `AffineSerreVanishing.affine_serre_vanishing`)
40	runs on: there Mathlib v4.31 provides *no* Grothendieck-abelian / enough-injectives instance
41	for `SheafOfModules`, so every derived-functor statement in that lane carries
42	`[EnoughInjectives X.Modules]` / `[HasInjectiveResolutions X.Modules]` as an un-instantiable
43	hypothesis.  The genus carrier deliberately uses the constant-`k` sheaf category precisely to
44	avoid that trap — and the trap is genuinely avoided.
45	
46	Consequence (`module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate`): gate 3 can simply be
47	dropped from the `N12` consumable — Mathlib synthesises it — leaving only gates 1, 2, 4.
48	
49	## Gate 4 (the comparison `∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso …`): NOT instantiable today
50	
51	`HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰` (`MayerVietorisCover.lean`) is the `Prop`-class packaging of the
52	comparison data `∀ n, cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F n (⨆ 𝒰)`, i.e. "for the cover
53	`𝒰`, unnormalised Čech cohomology equals derived (`Ext`) cohomology in every degree".
54	
55	For the 2-affine cover `S.coverFamily` this comparison is *mathematically* the Leray statement
56	"an affine cover is acyclic ⟹ Čech computes cohomology", which for a **two**-element cover is
57	exactly the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence (`HModule'_sequence_exact`, in-tree) together
58	with **affine Serre vanishing in the constant-`k` sheaf apparatus**:
59	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`, i.e. `Subsingleton (HModule' k
60	(toModuleKSheaf C) i U) = 0` for every affine open `U` and every `i > 0`.  Given that vanishing,
61	the comparison assembles degreewise: `n = 0` (sheaf axiom), `n = 1` (`cechCohomologyOneEquivH1Cok`
62	= node `N5`, in-tree, plus the MV cokernel identification), `n ≥ 2` (both sides vanish).
63	
64	The **precise gap** is therefore this single named input:
65	
66	> **MISSING:** `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` — Serre vanishing
67	> `Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_C) = 0` (`i > 0`, `U` affine) in the `Sheaf (Opens.gT …) (ModuleCat k)` apparatus,
68	> **plus** the degreewise assembly of the 2-cover comparison from it.
69	
70	Neither piece is a one-line consequence of an existing lemma:
71	
72	* Mathlib has no scheme-cohomology Serre vanishing at all, in any apparatus.
73	* The in-tree Serre vanishing `AffineSerreVanishing.affine_serre_vanishing` lives in the *wrong*
74	  category (`X.Modules`, `Ext (jShriekOU U)`) and is itself gated on the un-instantiable
75	  `[EnoughInjectives (Spec R).Modules]`; bridging it to the constant-`k` apparatus would need a
76	  "cohomology is independent of the linear structure" comparison that is likewise absent.
77	* The Čech-to-derived carrier `IsAffineHModuleVanishing` is currently *produced* in-tree only
78	  from `HasAffineCechAcyclicCover` — which itself bundles `HasCechToHModuleIso` on the affine
79	  sub-covers, i.e. the very comparison we are trying to instantiate (a circular producer).
80	
81	So gate 4 is a genuine multi-lemma target, **but the historical infrastructure blocker is gone**:
82	because `EnoughInjectives 𝒮` is now available (proved below), the honest way to close gate 4 is
83	to build affine Serre vanishing + the Čech comparison *directly in the constant-`k` sheaf
84	category* `𝒮` (where injective resolutions exist), rather than attempting to route through the
85	blocked `SheafOfModules` lane.  That is the recommended roadmap for the next wave.
86	
87	## Deliverable of this file
88	
89	* the gate-3 infrastructure, proved and named for citation
90	  (`isGrothendieckAbelian_moduleKSheaf`, `enoughInjectives_moduleKSheaf`,
91	  `hasExt_moduleKSheaf`, `hasExt_succ_moduleKSheaf`);
92	* the gate-3-free restatement of the `N12` consumable
93	  (`module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate`): under gates 1, 2, 4 alone,
94	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite `k`-module.  Once `P1ChartData` lands (gate 2) and the gate-4
95	  comparison is built, `Module.Finite k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` — hence the honesty of `genus C` — is
96	  unconditional on a curve with a finite map to ℙ¹.
97	-/
98	
99	universe u
100	
101	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
102	
103	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic
104	
105	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
106	
107	/-! ## Gate 3: the `Ext` infrastructure of the constant-`k` sheaf category is present -/
108	
109	/-- The genus-carrier sheaf category `Sheaf (Opens.gT X) (ModuleCat k)` is **Grothendieck
110	abelian**: sheaves valued in the Grothendieck-abelian `ModuleCat.{u} k` on the small site of
111	opens of `X`.  Mathlib's `IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v} (Sheaf J A)` fires here.  This is the
112	structural fact that makes the derived-functor genus apparatus well-founded (contrast the
113	`SheafOfModules 𝒪_X` apparatus, for which Mathlib v4.31 supplies no such instance). -/
114	theorem isGrothendieckAbelian_moduleKSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) :
115	    IsGrothendieckAbelian.{u}
116	      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
117	  inferInstance
118	
119	/-- The genus-carrier sheaf category has **enough injectives** (Stacks `079H`, from
120	Grothendieck-abelianness).  This is the input the entire `Ext`/derived-functor comparison
121	needs, and the exact instance the `SheafOfModules 𝒪_X` lane cannot supply.  Its availability
122	here is what dissolves the historical Čech-capstone blocker for the *constant-`k`* apparatus. -/
123	theorem enoughInjectives_moduleKSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) :
124	    EnoughInjectives
125	      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
126	  inferInstance
127	
128	/-- Gate 3, lower universe: `HasExt.{u}` for the genus-carrier sheaf category is synthesisable
129	(from `HasExt.standard`, itself from Grothendieck-abelianness). -/
130	theorem hasExt_moduleKSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) :
131	    HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
132	  inferInstance
133	
134	/-- Gate 3, upper universe: `HasExt.{u+1}` for the genus-carrier sheaf category is
135	synthesisable (the ambient `Ext`-theory the universe-bridged `HModule` genus carrier runs on). -/
136	theorem hasExt_succ_moduleKSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) :
137	    HasExt.{u+1} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :=
138	  inferInstance
139	
140	/-! ## Gate-3-free restatement of the genus-finiteness consumable (node `N12`)
141	
142	Because both `HasExt` gates are now synthesised (gate 3 above), the `N12` consumable of
143	`GenusFiniteness.lean` can be restated without them: the only remaining gates are the geometric
144	inputs (`HasFiniteMapToP1 C`, `P1HasLaurentChartData k`) and the Čech-to-derived comparison
145	(gate 4).  This is the honest, tightest current form of adelic genus finiteness. -/
146	
147	/-- **Genus finiteness of the curve, gate-3-free form (node `N12`).**  For a curve `C` over `k`
148	with a finite morphism to ℙ¹ and the ℙ¹ chart data, and with the Čech-to-derived comparison on
149	2-affine covers (gate 4), the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1` is a
150	finite `k`-module.  Identical to `Adelic.module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1` but with the
151	two `HasExt` hypotheses dropped — Mathlib synthesises them from the Grothendieck-abelianness of
152	the constant-`k` sheaf category (`hasExt_moduleKSheaf`, `hasExt_succ_moduleKSheaf`).  Once gates
153	2 and 4 are discharged, `Module.Finite k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` — and hence the honesty of `genus C` — is
154	unconditional on any curve with a finite map to ℙ¹. -/
155	theorem module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate
156	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] [P1HasLaurentChartData k]
157	    [∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare,
158	      HasCechToHModuleIso (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily] :
159	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 1) :=
160	  module_finite_hModule_one_of_finite_map C
161	    (fun S => ⟨S.hModuleOneEquivH1Cok (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C)⟩)
162	
163	end AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic

 Commit your work into the workspace ledger with a semantic message.            
                                                                                
 Provenance (run/session/role/task/projects) is stamped automatically from the  
 run environment; do not pass it. Commits only your files; the orchestrator

text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/Axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/project-git

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You never commit.** The orchestrator writes the integration commit for each
  session automatically. You *read* history; you do not commit project or
  workspace repos manually, and there is no "project VCS" to reconcile.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
To inspect Archon's history, drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.CechComparisonGate
7	
8	/-!
9	# Gate 4: the Čech-to-derived comparison on 2-affine covers, reduced to affine vanishing
10	
11	This file attacks **gate 4** of the unconditional genus-finiteness consumable
12	`Adelic.module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate`
13	(`CechComparisonGate.lean`), namely the instance
14	
15	```
16	∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily.
17	```
18	
19	`HasCechToHModuleIso F 𝒰` (`MayerVietorisCover.lean`) packages, for the cover `𝒰`, a
20	degreewise `k`-linear comparison
21	`∀ n, cechCohomology C F 𝒰 n ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F n (⨆ 𝒰)` between unnormalised Čech
22	cohomology and the `Ext`-based derived cohomology `HModule'`.
23	
24	## The mathematical reduction (Leray on a 2-affine cover)
25	
26	For the 2-affine cover `S.coverFamily` of a separated `k`-curve `C`, with the three
27	pieces `U₁`, `U₂`, `U₁ ⊓ U₂` affine (the `AffineCoverMVSquare` fields), the comparison
28	is the classical statement "an acyclic cover computes derived cohomology", which for a
29	**two**-element cover is the Mayer–Vietoris long exact sequence
30	(`HModule'_sequence_exact`, in-tree) fed by **affine Serre vanishing in the constant-`k`
31	sheaf apparatus** `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`, i.e.
32	`Subsingleton (HModule' k (toModuleKSheaf C) i U) = 0` for every affine open `U` and
33	every `i > 0`.  Given that vanishing the comparison assembles degreewise:
34	
35	* `n = 0`: sheaf axiom (`H⁰` on both sides is the group of global sections);
36	* `n = 1`: `AffineCoverMVSquare.cechCohomologyOneEquivH1Cok` (node N5, in-tree,
37	  unconditional) `cechCohomology C F S.coverFamily 1 ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok S F`, chained with the
38	  MV cokernel identification `H1Cok S F ≃ₗ[k] HModule' k F 1 ⊤` (which uses the
39	  degree-`0`/degree-`1` slice of the MV LES together with the affine `H¹`-vanishing on
40	  `U₁`, `U₂`);
41	* `n ≥ 2`: both sides vanish — the Čech complex of a 2-element cover is `3`-term, and the
42	  derived side vanishes by the MV LES together with the affine vanishing on
43	  `U₁`, `U₂`, `U₁ ⊓ U₂`.
44	
45	## What this file establishes
46	
47	* `AffineCoverMVSquare.isAffineOpen_coverFamily` / `isAffineOpen_overlapOpen`: the three
48	  pieces of the cover, in their `coverFamily`/`overlapOpen` typed forms, are affine
49	  (bridging the structure fields to the family-indexed forms the degreewise assembly
50	  consumes).
51	* `AffineCoverMVSquare.subsingleton_hModule'_coverFamily` /
52	  `subsingleton_hModule'_overlapOpen`: the **per-piece derived vanishing** — under
53	  `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C F`, `Subsingleton (HModule' k F i (piece))` for every
54	  `i > 0`.  These are the affine-vanishing inputs the Mayer–Vietoris degreewise assembly
55	  reads off (the `H¹` cokernel identification and the `n ≥ 2` whole-space vanishing are
56	  both immediate consequences of the MV LES fed by exactly these).
57	* `module_finite_hModule_one_unconditional`: the capstone, stated under the honest gate
58	  set (finite map to ℙ¹, ℙ¹ chart data, and the gate-4 comparison), delivering
59	  `Module.Finite k (H¹(C, 𝒪_C))`.  This is `module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1`
60	  with the `HasExt` gates synthesised (via `CechComparisonGate`); once the gate-4 instance
61	  is supplied — i.e. once `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` is proved and
62	  the degreewise assembly built — the genus of the curve is honest.
63	
64	## The precise residual
65	
66	The single named residual for the **unconditional** gate 4 is
67	
68	> `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` — affine Serre vanishing
69	> `Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_C) = 0` (`i > 0`, `U` affine) in the `Sheaf (Opens.gT …) (ModuleCat k)`
70	> apparatus —
71	
72	together with the degreewise assembly (the degree-`0`/degree-`1` MV cokernel
73	identification and the `n ≥ 2` whole-space vanishing) built from it.  No `sorry`/axiom or
74	sorried instance is introduced here; the residual is the existing `Prop`-class
75	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing`, whose producer for the structure sheaf is the genuine open
76	target (Mathlib supplies no scheme-cohomology Serre vanishing in this apparatus, and the
77	in-tree `X.Modules` vanishing is gated on the un-instantiable
78	`[EnoughInjectives (Spec R).Modules]`).
79	
80	**Universe note for the assembly (probe-confirmed here).**  The affine vanishing lives at
81	`HModule' = Abelian.Ext.{u}` (`Type u`), but the in-tree Mayer–Vietoris LES
82	`AffineCoverMVSquare.HModule'_sequence` has its `HasExt` baked at `Abelian.Ext.{u+1}`
83	(`Type u+1`): the two carriers are *not* definitionally equal, so the degreewise assembly
84	must transport the per-piece vanishing across the universe bridge
85	`Abelian.Ext.chgUnivLinearEquiv` (`MayerVietorisCore.lean`) before feeding it into the LES.
86	This is the same `Ext.{u}` ↔ `Ext.{u+1}` bridge the `HModule'`/`HModule` interface already
87	uses (`HModule'_eq_HModule_linearEquiv`), and is the one non-obvious wrinkle a future
88	author of the assembly must account for.
89	-/
90	
91	set_option autoImplicit false
92	
93	universe u
94	
95	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace AlgebraicGeometry AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
96	
97	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
98	
99	section Affineness
100	
101	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (S : X.AffineCoverMVSquare)
102	
103	/-- Each piece of the 2-element cover family is affine: `S.coverFamily i` is `U₁` or
104	`U₂`, both affine by the `AffineCoverMVSquare` fields. -/
105	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.isAffineOpen_coverFamily (i : ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) :
106	    IsAffineOpen (S.coverFamily i) := by
107	  rcases i with ⟨i⟩
108	  fin_cases i
109	  · exact S.isAffineOpen_U₁
110	  · exact S.isAffineOpen_U₂
111	
112	/-- The overlap `U₁ ⊓ U₂` of the 2-element cover, in the `overlapOpen` typed form used by
113	the degreewise Čech assembly, is affine. -/
114	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.isAffineOpen_overlapOpen :
115	    IsAffineOpen S.overlapOpen :=
116	  S.isAffineOpen_inf
117	
118	end Affineness
119	
120	/-! ## Per-piece derived-cohomology vanishing (the acyclicity inputs of the assembly)
121	
122	Under affine Serre vanishing `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C F`, each affine piece of the
123	2-affine cover has vanishing higher derived cohomology `HModule'`.  These are the exact
124	inputs the degreewise Čech comparison consumes (the Mayer–Vietoris LES on the cover reads
125	off `H¹(⊤)` and the higher vanishing from precisely these). -/
126	
127	section PieceVanishing
128	
129	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
130	  (S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare)
131	  (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))
132	  [HasExt.{u} (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology C.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
133	  [IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C F]
134	
135	/-- Higher derived cohomology of `F` vanishes on each piece `S.coverFamily j` of the
136	2-affine cover (both pieces are affine). -/
137	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.subsingleton_hModule'_coverFamily
138	    (j : ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
139	    Subsingleton (Scheme.HModule' k F i (S.coverFamily j)) :=
140	  IsAffineHModuleVanishing.subsingleton_HModule' (F := F) (S.isAffineOpen_coverFamily j) i hi
141	
142	/-- Higher derived cohomology of `F` vanishes on the overlap `U₁ ⊓ U₂` of the 2-affine
143	cover (the overlap is affine). -/
144	lemma AffineCoverMVSquare.subsingleton_hModule'_overlapOpen
145	    (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
146	    Subsingleton (Scheme.HModule' k F i S.overlapOpen) :=
147	  IsAffineHModuleVanishing.subsingleton_HModule' (F := F) S.isAffineOpen_overlapOpen i hi
148	
149	end PieceVanishing
150	
151	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
152	
153	/-! ## The capstone: genus finiteness under the honest gate set
154	
155	Once the gate-4 comparison instance
156	`∀ S, HasCechToHModuleIso (toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily` is available (its unconditional
157	production is the residual `IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)` plus the
158	degreewise assembly), the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is a finite `k`-module. -/
159	
160	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic
161	
162	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
163	
164	/-- **Genus finiteness of the curve, honest gate-set form.**  For a curve `C` over `k`
165	with a finite morphism to ℙ¹ (`HasFiniteMapToP1`), the ℙ¹ chart data
166	(`P1HasLaurentChartData`), and the Čech-to-derived comparison on 2-affine covers (gate 4),
167	the genus carrier `H¹(C, 𝒪_C) = HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 1` is a finite `k`-module.
168	
169	This is `module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate` (the `HasExt`-free
170	restatement, `CechComparisonGate.lean`) named as the lane capstone.  It becomes
171	**unconditional** exactly when gate 2 (`P1HasLaurentChartData k`, lane A) and gate 4
172	(this file's target instance, whose residual is affine Serre vanishing
173	`IsAffineHModuleVanishing k C (toModuleKSheaf C)`) are both discharged. -/
174	theorem module_finite_hModule_one_unconditional
175	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] [P1HasLaurentChartData k]
176	    [∀ S : C.left.AffineCoverMVSquare,
177	      HasCechToHModuleIso (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) S.coverFamily] :
178	    Module.Finite k (Scheme.HModule k (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf C) 1) :=
179	  module_finite_hModule_one_of_finiteMapToP1_of_cechGate C
180	
181	end AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic

52	noncomputable abbrev HModule
53	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
54	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}

60	identification of `HModule k F 0` with the Hom group from the constant
61	sheaf at `ModuleCat.of k k`. Mathlib provides
62	`CategoryTheory.Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀ : Ext X Y 0 ≃ₗ[R] (X ⟶ Y)` in any
63	`Linear R`-enriched abelian category; specialised to the `Linear k`
64	enrichment of `Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)` (auto-inferable from
65	`HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`), this collapses `HModule k F 0` to a

67	probe-confirmed one-liner (iter-010 plan-agent). Used downstream to
68	identify `H⁰(C, toModuleKSheaf C)` with `Γ(C, O_C)` viewed as a
69	`k`-module on a connected proper `k`-curve. -/
70	noncomputable def HModule_zero_linearEquiv

72	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
73	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
74	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) :
75	    HModule k F 0 ≃ₗ[k]
76	      ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F) :=
77	  Abelian.Ext.linearEquiv₀

79	/-- Phase A step 6 *Path 2* (iter-013 scaffold): the `ModuleCat k`-flavored
80	cohomology of an open `X : C` with values in a sheaf `F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)`.
81	Mirrors Mathlib's `Sheaf.H' F n X = (F.cohomologyPresheaf n).obj (op X)`
82	(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/SheafCohomology/Basic.lean` L105) for
83	`AddCommGrpCat`-valued sheaves, with `AddCommGrpCat.free → ModuleCat.free k`.
84	
85	The codomain is `Type u` (not `ModuleCat.{u} k`): `Abelian.Ext` returns a bare
86	`Type u` carrying `Module k` via `Abelian.Ext.instModule` through the `Linear k`
87	enrichment. The `noncomputable abbrev` form (rather than `def`) is required so
88	instance synthesis sees through the wrapper to find `Module k (HModule' k F n X)`
89	and `AddCommGroup (HModule' k F n X)` — under `def`, `Module.finrank` would fail

92	This is the prerequisite for the iter-014+ `ModuleCat k`-flavored Mayer-Vietoris

94	The iter-014+ work will state and prove the LES on a `MayerVietorisSquare`,

100	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}

102	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
103	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (n : ℕ) (X : C) : Type u :=
104	  Abelian.Ext ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
105	    ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X)) F n

122	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
123	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
124	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
125	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (X : C) :
126	    HModule' k F 0 X ≃ₗ[k]
127	      ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
128	        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X) ⟶ F) :=

132	H⁰ bridge `HModule_zero_linearEquiv : HModule k F 0 ≃ₗ[k] ((constantSheaf J _).obj
133	(ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F)` identifies the degree-zero cohomology with a `k`-linear Hom
134	group; Mathlib's `Module.Finite.equiv` then transports `Module.Finite k`-ness across.

136	Hom group on the RHS, but we want the Hom hypothesis on the LHS and the
137	`HModule` conclusion on the RHS, so we apply `.symm` first. Mirrors iter-037's

140	(HModule k (toModuleKSheaf C) 0)` once the Hom-from-constant-sheaf finiteness

142	theorem module_finite_HModule_zero
143	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
144	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
145	    [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)] [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
146	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))
147	    [Module.Finite k ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)).obj (ModuleCat.of k k) ⟶ F)] :
148	    Module.Finite k (HModule k F 0) :=
149	  Module.Finite.equiv (HModule_zero_linearEquiv k F).symm

152	of `Scheme.module_finite_HModule_zero` for the iter-014 sheaf-parameterised carrier
153	`HModule'`. The iter-015 H⁰ bridge `HModule'_zero_linearEquiv : HModule' k F 0 X ≃ₗ[k]
154	((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj ((yoneda ⋙ ModuleCat.free k).obj X) ⟶ F)` identifies the
155	degree-zero open-evaluation cohomology with a `k`-linear Hom group from the sheafified
156	representable; Mathlib's `Module.Finite.equiv` then transports `Module.Finite k`-ness
157	across. The `.symm` is required for the same orientation reason as in
158	`Scheme.module_finite_HModule_zero`. -/
159	theorem module_finite_HModule'_zero
160	    (k : Type u) [Field k]
161	    {C : Type v} [Category.{u, v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
162	    [HasWeakSheafify J (Type u)] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} k)]
163	    [HasExt (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k))]
164	    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} k)) (X : C)
165	    [Module.Finite k ((presheafToSheaf _ _).obj
166	        ((yoneda ⋙ (Functor.whiskeringRight _ _ _).obj (ModuleCat.free k)).obj X) ⟶ F)] :
167	    Module.Finite k (HModule' k F 0 X) :=

309	/-- Iter-044 geometric Stein input for the iter-043 wholespace H⁰
310	Hom-finiteness carrier. For `C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))` an
311	integral $k$-scheme with proper structure morphism, the global sections
312	$\Gamma(C, O_C)$ form a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space.

314	This is Stein's classical statement, packaged via Mathlib's
315	`AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed`
316	(`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/Proper.lean`):
317	for $X$ integral and $f \colon X \to \Spec K$ universally closed and
318	locally of finite type, the structure-morphism ring map `f.appTop`
319	is module-finite. `IsProper f` packages both `UniversallyClosed f` and
320	`LocallyOfFiniteType f`.

322	The bridge from `RingHom.Finite (C.hom.appTop.hom)` to
323	`Module.Finite k (C.left.presheaf.obj (op ⊤))` (where the algebra
324	structure on `Γ(C, ⊤)` is iter-006's `kToSection`-derived) uses
325	`RingHom.finite_algebraMap` plus `Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv` to
326	transport the base ring from intermediate `Γ(Spec k, ⊤)` to `k` along
327	the ring iso `Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)`. The compatibility
328	of algebra maps reduces to showing
329	`kToSection C (op ⊤).hom = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp (Scheme.ΓSpecIso _).inv.hom`,
330	which collapses via `Subsingleton.elim` on the `⊤ ⟶ ⊤` hom-set +

335	`constantSheafΓAdj.homEquiv` to a `LinearEquiv` + identification of
336	`Sheaf.Γ.obj (toModuleKSheaf C)` with the underlying global sections
337	+ transport via `Module.Finite.equiv`. -/
338	theorem module_finite_globalSections_of_isProper
339	    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
340	    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsProper C.hom] :
341	    Module.Finite k (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) := by
342	  have hf : (C.hom.appTop.hom).Finite :=
343	    AlgebraicGeometry.finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed k C.hom
344	  letI alg2 : Algebra ((Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
345	               (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
346	    := RingHom.toAlgebra C.hom.appTop.hom
347	  have hM_inter :
348	      Module.Finite ((Spec (CommRingCat.of k)).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
349	        (C.left.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) := by
350	    rw [← RingHom.finite_algebraMap]; exact hf
351	  refine Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv
352	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
353	    (RingEquiv.refl _) ?_
354	  ext x
355	  simp only [RingHom.coe_comp, RingEquiv.coe_toRingHom, RingEquiv.refl_apply,
356	    Function.comp_apply, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
357	  have h_kts : (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op ⊤)).hom =
358	                (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom) := by
359	    ext y
360	    simp only [Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection, CommRingCat.hom_comp,
361	      RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]
362	    exact congrFun (congrArg (·.hom) (C.left.presheaf.map_id (Opposite.op (⊤ :
363	                TopologicalSpace.Opens C.left.toTopCat)))) _
364	  calc (CommRingCat.Hom.hom (Scheme.toModuleKSheaf.kToSection C (Opposite.op ⊤)))
365	        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv x)
366	       = (C.hom.appTop.hom).comp ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv.hom)
367	          ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv x) :=
368	              congrFun (congrArg DFunLike.coe h_kts) _
369	    _  = C.hom.appTop.hom x := by
370	        simp only [RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply]
371	        congr 1
372	        change ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).hom ≫
373	              (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of k)).inv).hom x = x
374	        rw [Iso.hom_inv_id]; rfl

314	
315	The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
316	map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
317	`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
318	`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.
319	
320	Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
321	Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/

326	replaced by the **explicit** natural transformation `abelMapWitness C`, and the
327	class `HasAbelMap` is repinned to **carry the map itself** (a data field

329	property (`abelMap_app_mk` below) rather than being an opaque `Classical.choice`

333	a relative effective divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` on `C ×_k T` has invertible ideal
334	`I_D = ker q`; the Abel map sends its class to
335	`[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[I_D]`, the additive inverse (in the group-valued target
336	`Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`) of the class of the ideal sheaf.  It is assembled as the
337	composite `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`, where `abelKernelNatTrans` is the
338	substantive `[D] ↦ [I_D]` transformation and `picNeg` is the (natural)
339	negation on the group-valued functor.

343	**kernel–pullback comparison** `g_C^*(ker q) ⟶ ker(g_C^* q)` is an isomorphism

2155	\begin{thm}[Main]\label{th:main}
2156	 Assume $f\:X\to S$ is projective Zariski locally over $S$, and is flat
2157	with integral geometric fibers.
2158	
2159	\tu{(1)} Then $\IPic_{X/S}$ exists, is separated and locally of finite
2160	type over $S$, and represents $\Pic_{(X/S)\et}$.
2161	
2162	\tu{(2)} If also $S$ is Noetherian and $X/S$ is projective, then
2163	$\IPic_{X/S}$ is a disjoint union of open
2164	 subschemes, each an increasing union of open quasi-projective
2165	$S$-schemes.
2166	 \end{thm}
2167	
2168	\begin{proof}
2169	 By~\cite[(0, 4.5.5), p.~106]{EGAG}, it is a local matter on $S$ to
2170	represent a Zariski sheaf on the category of $S$-schemes.  Moreover, it
2171	is also a local matter on $S$ to prove that an $S$-scheme is separated
2172	and locally of finite type.  Hence, in order to prove (1), we may assume
2173	$S$ is Noetherian and $X/S$ is projective.
2174	
2175	Plainly an $S$-scheme is separated if it is a disjoint union of
2176	separated open subschemes, or if it is an increasing union of
2177	separated open subschemes.  Hence (1) follows from (2).
2178	
2179	To prove (2), owing to Yoneda's lemma, we may view the category of
2180	schemes as a full subcategory of the category of functors by identifying
2181	a scheme $T$ with its functor of points.  Denote this functor too by $T$
2182	in order to lighten the notation. And say that the functor is a scheme,
2183	as well as that it is representable.  Also, set
2184	 $$P:=\Pic_{(X/S)\et}.$$
2185	  Note $P(T)= \Hom(T,P)$. %% \{\,T\to P\,\}$.
2186	
2187	Given a polynomial $\phi\in\bb Q[n]$, let $P^\phi\subset P$ be the
2188	\'etale subsheaf associated to the presheaf whose $T$-points are
2189	represented by the invertible sheaves $\mc L$ on $X_T$ such that we have
2190	 \begin{equation}\label{eq:phi}
2191		\chi(X_t,\mc L^{-1}_t(n)) = \phi(n) \text{ for all $t\in T$}.
2192	 \end{equation}
2193	 Notice that this presheaf is well defined, because (\ref{eq:phi})
2194	remains valid after any base change $p\:T'\to T$; indeed, for any $t'\in
2195	T'$, for any $i$, and for any $n$, we have
2196		$$\uH^i\bigl(X_{t'},\mc L^{-1}_{t'}(n)\bigr)
2197	   =\uH^i\bigl(X_{p(t')},\mc L^{-1}_{p(t')}(n)\bigr)\ox_{k_t}k_{t'}$$
2198	 because cohomology commutes with flat base change by \cite[Prp.~III,
2199	9.3, p.~255]{Ha83}.  Hence $P^\phi$ is well defined too.
2200	
2201	Fix a map $T\to P$, and represent it by means of an \'etale covering
2202	$p\:T'\to T$ and an invertible sheaf $\mc L'$ on $X_{T'}$.  Consider the
2203	subset ${T'}^{\phi}\subset T'$ defined as follows:
2204	       $${T'}^{\phi}:=\{\,t'\in T'\mid
2205	       \chi\bigl(X_{t'},\mc L^{-1}_{t'}(n)\bigr) = \phi(n)\,\}.$$
2206	 Then ${T'}^{\phi}$  is  open by \cite[7.9.11]{EGAIII2}.
2207	
2208	Set $T^\phi:=p({T'}^{\phi})$.  Then $T^\phi\subset T$ is
2209	open as ${T'}^{\phi}\subset T'$  is  open and $p$ is  \'etale.
2210	
2211	Moreover, ${T'}^{\phi}=p^{-1}(T^\phi)$.  Indeed, let $t'\in
2212	p^{-1}(T^\phi)$.  Say $p(t')=p(t'_1)$ where $t'_1\in {T'}^\phi$.  Now,
2213	there is an \'etale covering $T''\to T'\x_TT'$ such that the two
2214	pullbacks of $\mc L'$ to $X_{T''}$ are isomorphic.  Let $t''\in T''$
2215	have image $t'\in T'$ under the first map $T''\to T'$ and have the image
2216	$t'_1\in T'$ under the second map.  Then
2217		$$\chi\bigl(X_{t'},\mc L^{-1}_{t'}(n)\bigr)
2218		 = \chi\bigl(X_{t''},\mc L^{-1}_{t''}(n)\bigr)
2219		 = \chi\bigl(X_{t'_1},\mc L^{-1}_{t'_1}(n)\bigr) = \phi(n).$$
2220	 Hence $t'\in {T'}^\phi$.  Thus ${T'}^{\phi}\supset
2221	p^{-1}(T^\phi)$. Therefore, ${T'}^{\phi}=p^{-1}(T^\phi)$.
2222	
2223	Furthermore, $T^\phi$ is (represents) the fiber product of functors
2224	$P^\phi\x_PT$.  Indeed, to see they have the same $R$-points, let
2225	$r\:R\to T$ be a map; form $R':=R\x_TT'$ and $r'\:R'\to T'$.  Suppose
2226	$r$ factors through $T^\phi$.  Then $r'$ factors through ${T'}^{\phi}$.
2227	So $R'\to T'\to P$ factors through $P^\phi$ essentially by definition.
2228	Now, $R'\to R$ is an \'etale covering.  Hence $R\to T\to P$ factors
2229	through $P^\phi$ since $P^\phi$ is an \'etale sheaf.
2230	
2231	Conversely, suppose $R\to T\to P$ factors through $P^\phi$.  Then $R\to
2232	P$ is defined by means of an \'etale covering $R''\to R$ and an
2233	invertible sheaf $\mc L''$ on $X_{R''}$ such that $\chi(X_u,\mc {\mc
2234	L''}^{-1}_u(n)) = \phi(n)$ for all $u\in R''$.  Since both $\mc L''$ and
2235	$\mc L'$ define $R\to P$, there is an \'etale covering $R'''\to
2236	R''\x_RR'$ such that the pullbacks of $\mc L''$ and $\mc L'$ to
2237	$X_{R'''}$ are isomorphic.  Hence the image of $r'\:R'\to T'$ lies in
2238	${T'}^{\phi}$.  But the latter is open.  Hence $r'$ factors through it.
2239	Therefore,   $r\:R\to T$ factors through $T^\phi$.  Thus  $T^\phi$ and
2240	$P^\phi\x_PT$ have the same $R$-points.
2241	
2242	Let $\phi$ vary.  Plainly the ${T'}^{\phi}$ are disjoint and cover $T'$.
2243	So the ${T}^{\phi}$ are disjoint and cover $T$.  Hence, by a general
2244	result~\cite[(0, 4.5.4), p.~103]{EGAG}, if the $P^\phi$ are
2245	(representable by) schemes, then $P$ is their disjoint union.  Thus it
2246	remains to represent each $P^\phi$ by an increasing union of open
2247	quasi-projective $S$-schemes.
2248	
2249	Fix $\phi$.  Given $m\in \bb Z$, let $P^\phi_m\subset P^\phi$ be the
2250	\'etale subsheaf associated to the presheaf whose $T$-points are
2251	represented by the $\mc L$ on $X_T$ such that, in addition to
2252	(\ref{eq:phi}), we have
2253	 \begin{equation}\label{eq:4b}

2280	images.  Therefore, by general principles, there is a natural
2281	isomorphism of functors
2282	 	$$ \tu R^{i-1}f_{\smash{T}*}(\mc L(n))_t\ox \mc N_t\risom
2283	 	 \tu R^{i-1}f_{\smash{T}*}\bigl(\mc L(n)\ox f_T^*\mc N\bigr)_t.$$

2296	P^\phi$, that, as $m$ varies, the products $P^\phi_m\x_{P^\phi}T$ form a

2298	argument, the key change is in proving openness.  In place of
2299	\cite[7.9.11]{EGAIII2}, we use the following part of Serre's
2300	Theorem~\cite[2.2.2]{EGAIII1}: given a coherent sheaf $\mc F$ on a

2302	many $i\ge1$ and $n\ge m$ such that $H^i(\mc F(n))$ is nonzero, and all
2303	these nonzero $A$-modules are finitely generated.  Hence, if there is a
2304	prime ${\bf p}$ of $A$ such that $H^i(\mc F(n))_{\bf p}=0$ for all

2312	isomorphism of functors $P^\phi_m \risom P^{\phi_0}_0$, which is defined

2330	$\theta(n):=\psi(n)-\phi_0(n)$.  Plainly $Z$ lies in
2331	$\IHilb_{X/S}^\theta(n)$, which is projective over $S$.  Hence $Z$ is

2338	$\alpha(\lambda_1)\in \smash{P_0^{\phi_0}}(T_1)$ is equal to the image of

Wave 1 of the representability campaign is now running. Summary of where things stand:

## Route decision (committed as `informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`, `9cd766fcf8`)

The judge scored three independent designs and picked the **Milne–Kollár architecture**: represent `Div^d` inside a Grassmannian (reusing the proved `Grassmannian.representable` + flattening substrate), use the rational-point section trick over a separably closed extension to carve `Pic^r` out of `Div^r` as an **equalizer** (a closed subscheme — no sheaf quotient at all), then descend by a **finite Galois quotient** (the only quotient in the whole proof, in the safe orbit-in-affine form) and assemble all degrees as a coproduct. The plan's three big pillars (B3 rigid pushforward engine, G2 Galois quotient engine, P5 uniform vanishing) are pairwise independent, and a 15-item blocking statement-audit checklist guards against the false-as-pinned traps that have burned this tree before.
